section: One Headline Number As The Title? Housing prices have increased ___ % over the past ___ years in the US
text:
One Headline Number As The Title? Housing prices have increased ___ % over the past ___ years in the US




Caption Text


At the aggregate, housing prices have increased from $122,626 to $366,157 from January of 2000 until September of this year, a 298.6% difference. This headline number, however, conceals variation in price at more granular geographies, and I am yet to explore how housing prices intertwine with rental prices and construction amount.
But how do the distributions of home value prices look? I want to use a histogram to look at this, as it can clearly show a distribution of a variable of discrete values.

 At the MSA level, housing prices are very positively skewed, meaning most MSAs have a lower average housing price; although there are many MSAs with much higher Avg housing price.

title: The Great Divergence In US Housing Prices
text:
Digging Deeper…
Graph about the correlation between housing construction and home prices (are there clear affects on the supply-side on housing prices? What about rental prices?) Look at the aggregate and then also at the state/MSA - Use a varying alpha from the correlation line, directly annotate the r on the graph



Caption Text


Note: I changed the alphas of the points to fade when further from the correlation, according to the findings of Strain et al. 
The correlation between housing prices and construction is 0.12, which is counter to what I would expect if supply-and-demand were to hold true (more construction leads to more supply which decreases price). There are some issues with this plot, namely that sampling is not independent (multiple MSAs show up in different years). Also, construction likely has some sort of lagged effect, perhaps into the next month or the next year. I want to create a plot or edit the data to reflect this lag (and also make independence valid) by looking at the change in housing prices (perhaps relative to the national trend?) following construction. I have to think about it more. Also how I can control for larger metros.
